# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b87 — Compact foldable dashboard and unclipped help

Beta87 is a **Lovelace presentation-only** update on top of Beta86. It retains all prior Home Environment Manager controllers, saved room/device settings, native error detection and announcements, PID adaptation and manual approvals, physical power-switch cooldown, and Home Assistant safety guards. No new device command, sensor, relay, authorization, or configuration migration is introduced.

## One-row home and outdoor conditions

- **One title row** for the Home Environment Manager title and existing home-configuration button; redundant subtitle/overline and decorative logo no longer consume vertical space.
- **Outdoor weather / warnings in at most two compact horizontal rows**: weather icon, safe/unsafe window guidance, temperature and wind on the first; AQI, other available readings and weather-warning indicators on one horizontally scrollable second row. Long reasons keep complete accessible hover/touch information and are not simply lost.
- **Room status overview is one horizontal bar**, replacing the large donut chart: total rooms, healthy, attention and missing-information counts with matching status icons.

## Collapsible rooms by default

Every monitored room starts **collapsed**, regardless of whether it is a normal room or a climate-only room. The one-line room summary preserves:
- Exact name, measured temperature and measured humidity (a dash for unavailable rather than an invented zero).
- Small icons for devices reporting actual physical activity; climate mode alone does **not** prove the equipment is running.
- Actionable icons for room warnings, open windows, unavailable data, device faults and paused/blocked equipment, with accessible descriptions.

Click the room heading (mouse, touch, Enter/Space) to expand. Expanded rooms still include the existing detailed metrics, climate panel, environmental calculations, shade controls, native windows, original sensor information and configuration entry points.

## Compact per-device summary and folded controls

Inside an expanded room, every managed device is collapsed by default and displays a one-line state/measurement summary:
- Physical operating state, the actual available temperature/humidity feedback, and PID demand when known.
- An icon for a real fault or for a paused/blocked controller, with a full diagnostic title.
- A single expansion arrow.

Opening a device reveals **all unchanged controls**: climate entity link, previous sensor tiles, device error details and per-device announce switch, Check and Continue, manual/automatic/PID selection, measured fan capacity, PID calibration, adaptive review and approval, window policy, and technical diagnostics. The card never infers a fault or activity from a blank attribute.

## Information bubbles remain on screen

The room/device info bubbles are now hosted in the browser's native **popover top layer** and positioned from the user's actual viewport. They are not clipped by the Home Environment Manager card boundary or adjacent Lovelace content, even when their original icon sits near the left or right edge. ESC / outside click closes a bubble. Supported browsers without the top-layer API receive an unclipped fixed-position fallback.

Native room/device expansion states survive ordinary HA state refreshes and do not replace or reset an unfinished dropdown or text edit. The existing full-screen source details and the built-in HA More Info action are preserved.

## Verification

- Real headless Chromium at widths **320, 360, 430 and 590 px**: two-row outdoor block, one-row overview, room and device collapsed/expanded behavior, important sensor and alarm icons, no horizontal page overflow, native dropdowns preserved, and unclipped popover geometry.
- Verified opening/closing room/device remains stable after Home Assistant redraws; no physical service call occurs during presentation.
- Previous Beta66/68/76/84/85/86 Chromium interaction regressions, device-fault/announcement routing, PID/automatic calibration, native command recovery, hardware minimum ON/OFF protections, occupancy and sleep/window controllers, all 38 shipped translations, JSON/Python/JavaScript syntax and Home Assistant event checks.

## Install

Update the existing HEM integration through HACS to **v0.6.0b87**, restart Home Assistant and perform a hard browser refresh. This is an interface-only release; all current room/device configuration, timers, last native fault reports and safety state continue to use the same records and entity identities.
